maya.docs: Heads-up I opened PR that combines the rate-limit migration guide + a short "how to read the dashboard" section. Includes a Python SDK snippet and a downloadable CSV widget example. Can someone sanity-check the billing/wording?

li.engineering: On it. Which Python snippet did you add? We try to show the client.meta.rate_limit structure now (snake_case in Python).

maya.docs: Yep, Python example uses client.call(...).meta.rate_limit. I also included a tiny fallback example for teams still parsing headers.

dave.billing: A couple product notes: 1) we adjusted the per-token price for Tier B last month; update numbers to $0.00035/token. 2) the quota export CSV includes separate columns for "committed_tokens" and "burst_tokens" now.

maya.docs: Thanks — updated price and CSV columns. Draft CSV header in docs: date,customer_id,model,committed_tokens,burst_tokens,total_tokens,cost_usd

rachael.analytics: For the dashboard widget query (for the quickstart), prefer this aggregate — it handles model aliases: ```sql
-- 7d window usage, split by committed vs burst
SELECT date_trunc('day', event_time) AS day,
       coalesce(customer_id, 'unknown') AS customer_id,
       coalesce(model_alias, model_id) AS model_name,
       sum(committed_tokens) AS committed_tokens,
       sum(burst_tokens) AS burst_tokens,
       sum(committed_tokens + burst_tokens) AS total_tokens
FROM redwood_usage.token_events
WHERE event_time >= now() - interval '7 days'
  AND event_type = 'generation'
GROUP BY day, customer_id, model_name
ORDER BY day DESC;
```

li.engineering: Nice. Two tiny infra nits: 1) we log burst usage as burst_tokens only on success events (so failed calls won't have burst recorded). Mention that in a footnote. 2) model_alias field may be NULL for older model versions. Good use of coalesce.

maya.docs: Added a footnote: "burst_tokens only present on successful generation events; failed requests report only attempted_tokens."

li.engineering: Also change Python snippet to use .meta.rate_limit and show reset_seconds. Current draft: ```py
# old header parsing
resp = client.generate(model='redwood-2', input='...')
headers = resp.headers
limit = int(headers.get('x-rw-ratelimit-limit', 0))
remaining = int(headers.get('x-rw-ratelimit-remaining', 0))
if remaining < 10:
    time.sleep(0.5)
```

li.engineering: Suggest replacing with: ```py
# recommended: use meta.rate_limit
resp = client.generate(model='redwood-2', input='...')
rl = getattr(resp, 'meta', {}).get('rate_limit', {})
# rl example: { 'limit': 600, 'remaining': 120, 'reset_seconds': 30, 'burst_used': 5 }
if rl and rl.get('remaining', 0) < 10:
    backoff = random.random() * rl.get('reset_seconds', 1) + 0.1
    time.sleep(backoff)
```

maya.docs: I'll swap that in and add a one-line migration note: "If you previously parsed X-RW-RATELIMIT-* headers, migrate to client response.meta.rate_limit (JS) or resp.meta.rate_limit (Python) — mapping examples provided."

dave.billing: Can you also add a short worked example: "If you have 200k committed tokens at Tier B ($0.00035/token) and use 250k tokens with 40k from burst, cost = 250k*$0.00035 = $87.50 and burst is free (not charged against committed)."

maya.docs: Added worked example and highlighted that bursts are not charged when configured as free bursts. Also added a note on metering granularity: we report input and output tokens separately, cost calc sums both.

rachael.analytics: For the CSV download widget docs, include the query and a note about timezone normalization (we normalize to UTC on export).

maya.docs: Done. Also added a short changelog entry "docs: migration guide for rate-limit headers -> meta.rate_limit; clarify burst accounting and update pricing numbers"

li.engineering: LGTM for infra accuracy.

dave.billing: LGTM for billing numbers.

maya.docs: Thanks all — will merge after CI green and then open a follow-up to port the Python examples to Go snippets. :shipit:
